$comment: Shared ladder fixture, consumed by BOTH ports: android MorseLadderTest and ios MorseKitCheck. Data, not code — see CLAUDE.md's two-ports rule.

derivation.studyOrder: kochOrder, then pickablePunctuation filtered to the opted-in set, in pickable order
derivation.note: History: Android threaded opted-in punctuation through the studyOrder ladder while iOS added it straight to the active set, and the ladder was chosen when the ports were reconciled. Reversed on 2026-09-11 (#213): a mark nobody could reach until all 37 core characters were mastered made the setting invisible. Opting in now adds the mark to the ACTIVE SET AT ONCE (optInCases) as well as keeping it on the ladder's tail (studyOrder unchanged, cases below), so it is drilled straight away and, being active, must be mastered like any other character before the next unlock.
derivation.optIn: activeAfter = activeBefore, then every pickablePunctuation character in selectedPunctuation that is not already active, appended at the end in pickable order; added = those characters in that order. Any active pickable mark NOT in selectedPunctuation is removed at the same time (removed, as in optOut). The mark's CharacterStats entry is created if it has none and kept if it has (behavioural check, not fixture data).
derivation.optOut: activeAfter = activeBefore with every pickablePunctuation character NOT in selectedPunctuation removed, relative order preserved; removed = those characters, in activeBefore order. Only pickable punctuation is ever removed: '?' is Koch core and stays, and a mark that was never earned is simply not there to remove. Opting back IN adds the mark straight back to the active set (optInCases). The mark's CharacterStats entry is kept on both ports (behavioural check, not fixture data).
derivation.optOutNote: Issue #133: opting out used to leave an earned mark in the drill. Decided: it is removed from the active set and its stats are kept, so opting back in and re-earning it loses no history.
derivation.fullPool: the games' 'Full alphabet and digits' set (#213): every kochOrder character in kochOrder order ('?' included, it is Koch core), then pickablePunctuation filtered to the opted-in set, in pickable order. Not ladder-gated: an opted-in mark is in it at once. Before #213 both ports filtered kochOrder to letters and digits, dropping '?' and ignoring the opt-in entirely.
derivation.fullPoolNote: Derived from the rule directly, independently of either implementation.
